"Less" refers to quantity, while "fewer" refers to number [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-004]. Therefore, "less" should not be misused in place of "fewer" when referring to countable items, such as men [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-003]. However, it is correct to use "less" with a round number that functions similarly to a collective noun, such as "less than a hundred" [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-004].
When *however* means "nevertheless," it should not come first in its sentence or clause [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p36-007].
